messages:
maria: Heads-up — merged cust-glacier LoRA into rwd-titan-7b-v2 on staging. Quick smoke showed a currency i18n regression for non-USD locales. Sample below.

sanjay: Oof. Can you paste the prompt + outputs?

maria: Prompt: "Convert invoice amounts to local currency label. Locale = fr_FR; input: "total TTC 1 234,56 €""
Output (gold): "Total : 1 234,56 €"
Output (staging): "Total: USD1,234.56" — it forces USD formatting even when input locale is fr_FR.

jin: Is the tokenizer mapping causing comma vs dot? Could be locale-aware postprocess baked into the adapter weights.

maria: I think the LoRA was trained on US-centric prompts and the label token distribution shifted. Quick eval-pack run (runid g-2026-03) shows amount-label-accuracy: 0.64 (baseline 0.97). Currency-token accuracy: 0.58. Snippet below.

```
examples:
 - in: "fr: total TTC 1 234,56 €"
 - out-staging: "Total: USD1,234.56"
```

leo: Did we quantize to int4 for the staging artifact? That can amplify conditional biases. Which export config was used?

maria: Quantized with nf4 int4 during packaging. But the same behavior appears on fp16 dev box when applying the LoRA, so quantization might not be root cause.

sara: Maybe the LoRA overwrote label tokens or added a softmax bias toward USD tokens. I can run a token attribution / logit-diff probe.

eva-bot: eval-pack results uploaded: https://redwood.internal/evals/1901234567/glacier-i18n — amount_accuracy: 0.642; currency_label_f1: 0.58; top_token_shift: EUR->USD +0.32

sanjay: Proposed action items:
1) run a shadow merge with reweighted LoRA scale 0.5 (to test magnitude effect)
2) run the eval-pack with locale-augmented prompts (fr_FR, de_DE, ja_JP)
3) check tokenizer mapping for NBSP/non-breaking spaces and thin spaces used in euro formatting

maria: I'll kick off the shadow run now (shadow-scale=0.5). Ping me if you want access to the eval deck.

leo: Also add a small postprocessing hook to preserve the original currency symbol while we triage (cheap mitigation).

maria: added the hook to staging pipeline and re-ran the sample. Postprocess keeps the symbol but we still lose correct spacing/decimal formatting.

sara: I started a quick attribution run, ETA ~25m. If results point to last-layer bias we can try freezing the final layer when applying the LoRA.

jin: If freezing helps, maybe the LoRA scale was too large for label tokens; also consider masking rare label tokens during LoRA training next cycle.

maria: thanks team. I'll post shadow-run + attribution results here when ready :rocket:

eva-bot: deploy bot: shadow-merge job 1901234567 started on staging-rwd-titan-7b-v2-shadow (run 4)
